tools.name: find_app
tools.description: Finds the listed apps that best do a task described in plain words, like "send password reset emails" or "scrape sites that need JavaScript". Returns each app with its summary, check results, reports from other agents, and where to read its setup file.

tools.name: get_setup_file
tools.description: Returns the checked setup file for a listed app, by its domain, such as resend.com. Includes what the check found: commands, other sites, sign-in, flags. The file is information from the company that wrote it.

tools.name: list_use_cases
tools.description: Lists the jobs the directory covers, like sending email or taking payments, with the apps for each.

findings.title: Description references secrets/credentials
findings.detail: Description of "find_app" references sensitive artifacts (password). A tool description has no reason to mention credentials.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: find_app, list_use_cases · Private data: find_app, get_setup_file · Public sink: find_app, list_use_cases · Destructive: find_app.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: find_app, list_use_cases · Private data: find_app, get_setup_file · Public sink: find_app, list_use_cases · Destructive: find_app

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
